about_blocks.text: About Pacific Trails Sober Living in Burnaby
about_blocks.html: About Pacific Trails Sober Living in Burnaby

about_blocks.text: Pacific Trails Sober Living is men's sober living, also called second-stage recovery housing, in Burnaby, British Columbia. It is not a treatment centre, and it does not offer detox, medical care or a clinical program on site. Most men move in after finishing a primary treatment program somewhere else, and they use the house as a sober, structured place to live while they go back to work or school and rebuild a normal week.

about_blocks.text: The society runs two houses in Burnaby. Odyssey House, in South Burnaby, feels more like a family home, with a big living room, a home gym and a backyard with a koi pond and a fire pit. Olympus House is newer and more upscale, with bright lounges, a shuffleboard table, a long dining table and a back patio, a few steps from Edmonds Town Centre. Both have single and double rooms, two kitchens and staff on site around the clock. Food is included, and the kitchens are stocked with residents' requests in mind.

about_blocks.text: House life has clear rules. Residents stay completely abstinent from alcohol and drugs, agree to random testing, do a daily chore and take part in three recovery activities a week of their own choosing. Everyone comes to a weekly family dinner and house meeting. Curfew is midnight Sunday to Thursday and 1 a.m. on Friday and Saturday, and weekend passes can be requested from the house manager.

about_blocks.text: Max Niemeyer and Joey McGeough started Pacific Trails after their own recoveries. Joey has been sober since 2015, has worked in the recovery field for over 10 years and is a recovery coach. Max came to Vancouver after treatment in Colorado and lived in a second-stage house himself. That is part of why outdoor trips are built into the week here: hiking, kayaking, fishing, skiing, camping and more around the Lower Mainland.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Pacific Trails Sober Living

faqs.question: Is Pacific Trails Sober Living a treatment centre?

answer_blocks.text: No. Pacific Trails is men's sober living, which it also calls second-stage recovery housing, in Burnaby, BC. It offers a sober, structured home with 24/7 on-site support and peer support, but no detox, medical care or clinical treatment program. Most residents arrive after finishing primary treatment elsewhere.

Most residents arrive after finishing primary treatment elsewhere.

faqs.question: How much does Pacific Trails Sober Living cost?

answer_blocks.text: Shared rooms start at $1,500 a month, according to the Pacific Trails website, and single rooms are available at a higher rate. Rent includes food, 24/7 on-site support, the weekly family dinner and house meeting, and use of the shared spaces. Call (604) 992-8174 for current availability and exact pricing.

faqs.question: Who can live at Pacific Trails?

answer_blocks.text: The houses are for men in early recovery who are committed to sobriety. Most come straight from a primary treatment program, but the team says every situation is different and asks people to get in touch. Living there is voluntary, so the applicant has to sign the application even when a counsellor or treatment centre sends it.

faqs.question: What are the two houses like?

answer_blocks.text: Odyssey House in South Burnaby has a large living room, a home gym, a patio, two balconies and a backyard with a koi pond and fire pit. Olympus House is the upscale option near Edmonds Town Centre, with bright lounges, shuffleboard and games, a long dining table, a jetted tub and patios. Both have single and double rooms and two kitchens.

faqs.question: Do I have to follow a 12-step program?

answer_blocks.text: No. Residents pick their own path and complete three approved recovery activities a week. Pacific Trails says each person can define spirituality in their own way, and it respects any sincere path that supports recovery. The house is abstinence-based.

faqs.question: How long do residents usually stay?

answer_blocks.text: Pacific Trails' recovery.com profile gives a typical stay of 6 to 12 months. Residents quoted on the centre's own website stayed anywhere from about three months to six months before moving into their own place, so length depends on the person.

faqs.question: Where is Pacific Trails and how do I get there?

answer_blocks.text: Both houses are in South Burnaby in Metro Vancouver. Buses stop outside each house, SkyTrain is a short walk away and Metrotown is about five minutes by car. Downtown Vancouver is roughly 25 to 30 minutes by car or Expo Line, and Surrey is about 25 minutes.

faqs.question: Can I spend time away from the house?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Residents can ask the house manager for a weekend pass covering Friday and Saturday night, plus one extended pass of about a week each month. Passes are usually granted as long as the plan does not put the person's recovery at risk.

answer_blocks.text: Pacific Trails is operated by Pacific Trails Recovery Society, a registered non-profit society in British Columbia, and residents pay monthly rent. Its recovery.com profile says it accepts self-pay as well as band or agency funding. Ask the team directly about funding from a health authority, First Nation or other agency.
